disease_label_per_paper: Fatal community-acquired MSSA aortic valve acute endocarditis associated with persistent Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, purulent pericarditis, rhabdomyolysis, and intracerebral hematoma
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 36-year-old man was admitted on illness day 4 with malaise, chills, low-grade fever, sweating, intense myalgia/arthralgia, purpuric exanthem, and diastolic murmur.
Initial vital signs included heart rate 130/min, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, axillary temperature 36.8 degC, and oxygen saturation 95%.
Blood cultures over admission and the next 2 days grew MSSA; aortic valve vegetations, severe aortic insufficiency, pericardial collections, and cerebral lesions developed rapidly.

Persistent MSSA bacteremia continued despite therapy; the patient developed oligoanuria requiring hemofiltration, coma with intracerebral hematoma, acute respiratory failure/ARDS, recurrent pericardial collection, and died on hospital day 19.
